warfarin.known: On warfarin for a heart valve
warfarin.say: I take warfarin for my heart valve. The blood thinner.

results.bloods: INR 3.6. The blood is thinner than it should be, even for a valve.

brain_bleed.right: CT now, reverse the warfarin at once with vitamin K and prothrombin complex, keep the blood pressure down, and call neurosurgery
brain_bleed.why: A bleed around the brain in someone on warfarin keeps growing until the blood can clot again. Reversing the warfarin comes first, then neurosurgery.
brain_bleed.trap_why: Right for a bleed, but on warfarin the blood can't clot. Without reversing it, the bleed keeps growing.

head_injury.right: CT head now, check the INR, and admit to watch overnight even though the scan is clear
head_injury.why: A head injury on warfarin can bleed slowly, hours later. A clear first scan isn't enough: check how thin the blood is and watch overnight.
head_injury.trap_why: On warfarin, a bleed can show up hours after a clear scan. Sent home tonight, they can come back unconscious.

nosebleed.right: Lean forward and pinch the soft part of the nose, check the INR, pack the nose if it keeps going, and ask the heart team before touching the warfarin
nosebleed.why: On warfarin, a nosebleed that seems to stop starts again at home. Find out how thin the blood is, pack it if needed, and never stop a valve patient's warfarin without the heart team.
nosebleed.trap_why: On warfarin, the bleeding starts again on the way home. Check the INR and be ready to pack the nose.

pregnant.say: I'm five months pregnant. First baby.

hidden.say: Nothing else. My period's a bit late, but that's just stress.

renal_colic.right: Paracetamol and, if needed, a small dose of morphine instead of diclofenac, an anti-sickness that's safe in pregnancy, an ultrasound rather than a CT, admit, and tell the obstetrician
renal_colic.why: A kidney stone in pregnancy: diclofenac-type painkillers are avoided because of the baby, and an ultrasound replaces a CT. The obstetrician should know.
renal_colic.trap: A diclofenac injection and an anti-sickness one, then home with tablets, plenty of water and a urology check
renal_colic.trap_why: She's pregnant. Diclofenac-type painkillers can harm the baby. Paracetamol, a small dose of morphine if needed, and the obstetrician told.

results.urine: Blood in the urine, no infection. Pregnancy test positive.

scrub_typhus.right: Azithromycin instead of doxycycline, paracetamol and fluids, admit, and tell the obstetrician
scrub_typhus.why: Scrub typhus in pregnancy is treated with azithromycin, which is safe for the baby. Doxycycline is avoided.
scrub_typhus.trap_why: She's pregnant. Doxycycline is avoided in pregnancy; azithromycin treats scrub typhus safely.

hepatitis.right: Admit, check the clotting and the sugar every few hours, and get the obstetricians in
hepatitis.why: Hepatitis E is mild for most people, but in pregnancy it can turn into liver failure, quickly. She needs watching in hospital.
hepatitis.trap_why: In pregnancy, hepatitis E can turn into liver failure within days. Home is the wrong place for her.

steroids.known: On steroid tablets for years, for arthritis
steroids.say: I take steroid tablets every day for my joints. Prednisolone. For years.

gastro.right: The drip and the anti-sickness injection, plus hydrocortisone through the drip until they keep their steroid tablets down, and admit overnight
gastro.why: After years on steroids the body can't make its own. Vomiting the tablets up can tip them into a crisis with falling blood pressure, so the steroid goes in through the drip.
gastro.trap_why: They've been vomiting up their steroid tablets. After years on them, the body can't cope without; they can come back in shock tonight.

perforated_ulcer.right: Nothing by mouth, a drip, antibiotics, pain relief, a stomach tube and extra hydrocortisone to cover the operation, and the surgeons for theatre now
perforated_ulcer.why: A burst ulcer in someone on long-term steroids, which may have helped cause it. The operation needs extra hydrocortisone, or the blood pressure can crash.
perforated_ulcer.trap_why: After years of steroids, going into a big operation without extra hydrocortisone can make the blood pressure crash.

ckd.known: Kidney disease, not yet on dialysis
ckd.say: My kidneys are weak. The kidney doctor checks me every three months.

renal_colic.right: Paracetamol and a small dose of morphine instead of diclofenac, an anti-sickness injection, an ultrasound, and the kidney team told
renal_colic.why: Weak kidneys and a stone: diclofenac-type painkillers can push weak kidneys into failure. Pain relief that spares them, and the kidney team in the loop.
renal_colic.trap: A diclofenac injection and an anti-sickness one, then home with tablets, plenty of water and a urology check
renal_colic.trap_why: Their kidneys are already weak. Diclofenac can tip them into failure.

results.bloods: Creatinine 3.3, about their usual. White count normal.

alcohol.say: I drink. Every day. A quarter, sometimes a half.

hidden.say: Drink? No, no. Only at weddings. Small one.

alcohol.exam: Smells of alcohol. A fine tremor in the hands. The liver edge can be felt.

hypoglycaemia.right: Thiamine with the dextrose through the drip, then a meal, recheck the sugar, sort out the insulin, and a talk about the drinking
hypoglycaemia.why: Low sugar in someone who drinks every day: sugar alone can bring on Wernicke's, a brain injury from too little thiamine. Give thiamine with the dextrose.
hypoglycaemia.trap_why: In someone who drinks every day, dextrose without thiamine can bring on Wernicke's, a lasting brain injury.

head_injury.right: CT head now, and admit to watch overnight even if it's clear, without putting any drowsiness down to the drink
head_injury.why: Drink hides the warning signs of a bleed, and people who drink every day bleed more easily. Scan, and watch overnight.
head_injury.trap_why: In a heavy drinker, a bleed can hide behind 'he's just drunk'. Sent home, he can come back unconscious.

pancreatitis.right: Admit, plenty of fluids through the drip, strong pain relief, thiamine, and a plan for alcohol withdrawal
pancreatitis.why: Pancreatitis in someone who drinks every day: as well as fluids and pain relief, he needs thiamine and a withdrawal plan, or he'll be shaking and seeing things by tomorrow night.
pancreatitis.trap_why: He drinks every day. Without thiamine and a withdrawal plan, he'll be shaking and seeing things within a day or two.

penicillin.say: Oh, and penicillin. Last time my whole face swelled up.

pneumonia.right: Oxygen, a non-penicillin antibiotic through the drip because of the allergy, fluids, and admit
pneumonia.why: Pneumonia in someone whose face swelled up with penicillin: the antibiotic comes from another family. Asking about allergies is never optional.
pneumonia.trap: Oxygen, co-amoxiclav through the drip, fluids, and admit
pneumonia.trap_why: They told you: penicillin swells their face up. Co-amoxiclav is a penicillin.

diabetic_foot.right: Admit, a non-penicillin antibiotic through the drip because of the allergy, insulin for the sugar, and the surgeons to clean the wound
diabetic_foot.why: An infected diabetic foot in someone allergic to penicillin: the antibiotic comes from another family. Always ask before you write the drip chart.
diabetic_foot.trap: Admit, co-amoxiclav through the drip, insulin for the sugar, and the surgeons to clean the wound
diabetic_foot.trap_why: They told you: penicillin swells their face up. Co-amoxiclav is a penicillin.

palm_rash.name: palm-rash fever
palm_rash.board: Fever with a rash on the palms
pain: Fever and a rash on my palms and soles. Itchy, like ants walking.
Fever, and these pink spots on my hands and feet. They itch like mad.
palm_rash.exam: Pink spots on the palms and soles. Glands up in the neck. Throat a little red.
palm_rash.bloods: White count low, 3,200. Liver enzymes a little raised. Nothing else stands out.

tin_mouth.name: tin-mouth fever
tin_mouth.board: Fever with red eyes and a metal taste
pain: Fever, and my eyes are red and watery. Everything tastes like metal. Even chai.
High fever, red eyes, and my food tastes like I'm chewing coins.
tin_mouth.exam: Red eyes without discharge. A coated tongue. Small glands behind the ears.
tin_mouth.bloods: White count low, 2,900. Platelets a little low, 118,000. Nothing else stands out.

pen_drop.name: pen-drop fever
pain: Fever, and my fingers are so stiff I can't hold a pen. Toes too.
High fever, and every small joint in my hands is stiff and puffy.
pen_drop.exam: Puffy, tender finger joints. A faint lacy rash on the arms. Glands up in the armpits.
pen_drop.bloods: White count low, 3,400. CRP a little raised. Nothing else stands out.

hiccup.name: hiccup fever
hiccup.board: Fever with hiccups that won't stop
pain: Fever, and I can't stop hiccuping. Two days of hiccups. My family is losing its mind.
High fever and hiccups every few seconds. I can't sleep, I can't eat, I can't talk properly.
hiccup.exam: Hiccuping every few seconds. A red throat with small blisters at the back. Glands up in the neck.
hiccup.bloods: White count low, 3,100. Sodium a little low. Nothing else stands out.

Since yesterday. Four people in my office are off with it.

Two days. My whole building has it. The watchman too.

I'm usually fit. I play cricket every Sunday. Well, I watch cricket every Sunday.
No medicines. The chemist says it's the new fever going around.
outbreak.label: Invented illness, made up for the game

plans.text: Isolate them, fluids and paracetamol, take samples for the lab, and report the cluster to the public health team
plans.why: This illness is invented for the game, but the way it's handled is real: a cluster of the same new fever is isolated, supported with fluids and paracetamol, sampled, and reported to the public health surveillance team, who track down the cause.

plans.text: Antibiotics for everyone who has it
plans.why: Invented illness, real lesson: guessing antibiotics for an unknown fever cluster doesn't treat a virus, breeds resistance and hides the cause.

plans.text: Steroids to bring the fever down
plans.why: Invented illness, real lesson: steroids for an unknown fever can let an infection run riot.

plans.text: Paracetamol and home, it's just a viral fever
plans.why: Invented illness, real lesson: one viral fever goes home, but the fifth patient with the same new fever this week is a cluster. Clusters get isolated and reported.

outbreak.news: District health office: a cluster of {board_low} is going round town. Hospitals are isolating and reporting cases. This illness is invented, made up for the game.
